name: Dunmer
description: The Dark Elves of Morrowind — ash-bred, kin-bound and proud, distrustful of outlanders.
lore: Descendants of the Chimer, changed by Azura's curse after the Battle of Red Mountain.

name: Altmer
description: The High Elves, long-lived and innately magical, heirs to a golden age.
lore: The Altmer claim descent from the Aldmer themselves; their arrogance is legendary and well-earned.

name: Bosmer
description: The Wood Elves of Valenwood — nimble, curious and bound to the Green Pact.
lore: The Green Pact forbids them harming the plants of their homeland, which shapes all they eat and build.

name: Orsimer
description: The Pariah Folk of Trinimac — mighty smiths and warriors, ever in exile.
lore: Changed by the corruption of their god Trinimac into Malacath, the Orcs endured contempt and built strongholds in the mountains.

name: Khajiit
description: The cat-folk of Elsweyr, born in many forms under the moons.
lore: A Khajiit's form — from the house-cat Alfiq to the battle-born Senche — is fixed by the phase of the moons at birth.

name: Argonian
description: The lizard-folk of the marsh, loyal to the Hist and gifted by its sap.
lore: Argonians are born of the Hist's influence; their memory is the memory of the swamp.

name: Nord
description: The proud, cold-bitten people of Skyrim, descended from the Atmoran conquerors of old.
lore: They claim Talos as kin and Kyne as patron; their songs remember wars older than the Empire.

name: Breton
description: The graht-kin of High Rock — fey-blooded, magic-resistant heirs of the Direnni.
lore: Breton blood carries elven sorcery of old; their knights and mages shaped the fractured kingdoms of the Iliac Bay.

name: Redguard
description: The sword-singers of Hammerfell, descended from the Yokudans who fled their sunken land.
lore: They refuse the Imperial identity, keep their own gods, and remember the Walkabout across the ocean.

name: Imperial
description: The cosmopolitan men and women of Cyrodiil, heirs to the Alessian and Septim Empires.
lore: The Imperials bind a hundred peoples together — their tongue is the common speech of Tamriel.
